MT-1cr|us1.basis: pin load along the governing 3D cradle leg (40 mm belly, 53 kg float limit, factored 1.6 g x 1.5); last step = the factored row

T1|us1.basis: T1 carry: bag-on cam-tight strap (drape path) at 1 g, scaled to the carry load (0 / 150 / 300 lb); local pin load only

MT-1cr|us2.basis: pin load along the governing 3D cradle leg (40 mm belly, 53 kg float limit, factored 1.6 g x 1.5); last step = the factored row

T1|us2.basis: T1 carry: bag-on cam-tight strap (drape path) at 1 g, scaled to the carry load (0 / 150 / 300 lb); local pin load only

CLEVIS-SHARE|us2_inboard.basis: CLEVIS-SHARE A: governing inboard leg; static proof = factored row, cycle peak = x 1.6 / 2.4 (1e5 cycles, R 0.1)
CLEVIS-SHARE|us2_inboard.eye_bears_on: inner (body) cheek: PTFE shim between the eye and the inner cheek's throat face

CLEVIS-SHARE|us2_yz.basis: CLEVIS-SHARE B: the leg with no lateral part (a load as wide as the span), contact 95 mm aft: all of it in y-z, the clevis's share-1.0 case; static proof = factored row, cycle peak x 1.6 / 2.4
CLEVIS-SHARE|us2_yz.eye_bears_on: outer (clevis) cheek, PTFE shim between the eye and the outer cheek (share 1.0 case)

pins.scheme: headed pin, R-clip through a cross hole on the far side, pin + clip on one tether

retainer.part: hitch-pin (R-) clip, 302 / 18-8 stainless, 1.2 mm wire, for 4.8-6.4 mm (3/16-1/4 in) pins
retainer.source: https://www.mcmaster.com/products/hitch-pin-clips/ (secondary: catalogue page not fetched; any 18-8 R-clip in that size range)
retainer.tether: 1.5 mm Dyneema (UHMWPE) cord, 120 mm, through the pin head's 1.6 mm hole and the clip's eye, larks-head round the stay beside the fairlead: pin and clip stay on the frame when pulled

us1.clip_side: inboard (towards x 0; the buttress leaves a 12 mm slot)

us2.clip_side: inboard (towards x 0; the buttress leaves a 12 mm slot)

pins.booked_before: bag_attach: 7075 pins 36 mm shank + 8 mm head (no retainer); Ti hinge 5 x 44

steps: (a) every pin in, clip seated: a 50 N push on the pin's tail along its axis (spring scale) moves it < 0.5 mm
(b) after the T9 walk and the MT-1cr / CLEVIS-SHARE cycles: every pin home, every clip fully seated, no wire wear groove deeper than 0.1 mm
(c) bag-off: each hinge pin out and back in by hand, gloved, clip off and on, <= 8 s each

orientation.all_files: as exported: the STL's z is the build direction (frame y up: wearer face down, bag face up). Do not rotate or flip on the plate: the FEA assumes the layers normal to frame y
orientation.why_not_flipped: bag face down needs as much support (lower 13 859 vs 11 164 mm2, upper 19 915 vs 18 044 mm2 supported area) and puts the support scars on the stays' bag faces and the fairlead tips (eye bearing, HE fit) instead of the wearer faces
orientation.test_pieces: print every test piece exactly like the frame (same orientation, same supports) so it carries the frame's surfaces and scars

supports.type: tree supports from the build plate only ('on build plate only'), auto, threshold 45 deg
supports.material: PAHT-CF itself (single nozzle H2S), no breakaway material
blockers: every pin hole and fairlead throat (12 stations)
both z 234 joint bores, counterbores and nut traps
the two US2 clevis bolt holes, counterbores and hex nut traps (body side)
the pawl bore and the spine channel
supports.note: a slicer that auto-supports everything puts supports inside the bores: paint blockers first

us2_clevis_R.stl / us2_clevis_L.stl.supports: none (prints flat: 97 % of the footprint on the plate)

scars.where: support contact lands on wearer-facing (-y) surfaces only: the stays' wearer faces (2224 + 8755 mm2) and the undersides of the lugs, fairlead roots and lane blocks; the lugs' governing spots (US1 outer cheek / floor corner, US2 arm root bag face, hinge inboard cheek corner) face up or sideways and carry no scar
scars.finish: sand the support witness on the stays' wearer faces and the lug undersides flat with 240 then 400 grit, removing at most 0.2 mm (SAND-ALLOW); deburr every bore edge

allowance.note: 0.2 mm off one face of an 18 mm deep stay (ASSUMPTION: rectangular-equivalent) costs about 2.2 % of its bending section modulus; the body's fatigue minimum on the sim bases (1.258, h1_crown) becomes about 1.23

print_settings.time_rule: (part + support volume) / 8 mm3/s x 1.08 (h1_buckling print_h rule)

assumptions.text: The under-strap meets the quarter 0-50 mm aft of the pin line (taut strap on the front edge against the spreader; a rounder bottom further aft): the design rows. 95 mm (half the quarter proxy's 190 mm depth) is run as a sensitivity.
assumptions.settled_by: MT-1cr with a >= 50 kg quarter-shaped load: photograph the strap contact line from the side and measure its distance aft of the pin line.

assumptions.text: The load in the cradle is the 280 mm wide R-08 quarter proxy (huntkit/viz3d/params.py): US1's legs run outboard to its edges, US2's straight down at its edge; a narrow load takes both legs inboard to x 0.
assumptions.settled_by: MT-1cr: legs' lateral direction at each pin, narrow (boned bag) and wide (bone-in) loads.

assumptions.text: The cradle is designed down to a 40 mm belly at the 53 kg float limit; flatter is not credited. A hand can reach it (5th-percentile male one-arm pull 178-199 N, FAA HFDS Ch. 14 Exh. 14.5.2.1; a strong user, both hands or a braced foot pull more), so no strength cap on the hand is used.
assumptions.settled_by: MT-1cr: cam each strap as hard as a strong user can, gloved, with the 53 kg load: belly measured >= 40 mm.

assumptions.text: The print submodel is fixed where its box cuts the frame (US1: x -6..140 incl. the lumbar hub; US2: x 80..192); the smaller boxes gave LESS severe US1 numbers (sensitivity in the record).
assumptions.settled_by: Strain gauges at the arm roots in MT-1cr (gauge table): measured <= the pass line.

assumptions.text: Outer cheek's share of the pin's y-z load 0.6 (1.0 as sensitivity); the inboard leg's x pull bears on the INNER (body) cheek and loads no clevis bolt.
T1 gauge values carry only the local bag-on pin load (the submodel has no global stay stress); the T1 pass line is advisory, MT-1cr and CLEVIS-SHARE (pin loads only) are the gates.
assumptions.settled_by: Record T1 anyway; compare with the whole-body model when it is re-run on the BL-053 body.

assumptions.text: Tree supports use 12 % of the column volume they span (+ 3 dense 0.2 mm interface layers); high estimate 25 %.
assumptions.settled_by: Bambu Studio plate preview of each file with the README's support settings: filament and time.

assumptions.text: Sanding the support witness off the stays' wearer faces removes <= 0.2 mm (about 2.2 % of the stay's bending section modulus).
assumptions.settled_by: Caliper the stay depth at 5 points before / after sanding on the first article.

assumptions.text: Support witness sanded flat costs no more fatigue strength than the 2.2 % section loss.
assumptions.settled_by: CA-1: add 2 XY bars printed over tree supports and sanded as the README says, against 2 printed flat.

assumptions.text: The strap's wrap over its own lug carries the bag-on cam-tight tension (US1 444 N, US2 296 N, factored 3.0) on the recorded meat drapes; the eye is necked to 18 mm in the throat.
assumptions.settled_by: FIT-US: inspect the lip and strap for fuzz or whitening after the crank cycles.

assumptions.text: The whole-body check (h1_buckling.full_check) was not re-run on the BL-053 body: the fixes are local lug blocks (+56 g) away from the governing body regions (lumbar struts, stay L lower sleeve z 160-240).
assumptions.settled_by: Re-run h1_crown --body on the BL-053 print body (heavy job, about an hour) before P1.
